rules.name: Inflated importance language
rules.description: Phrases that announce significance without showing why it matters.
rules.message: The wording claims importance more strongly than the surrounding evidence supports.
rules.suggestion: Replace the claim of importance with the observable consequence.

rules.name: Inflated copula alternative
rules.description: Writers sometimes avoid plain 'is' and 'has' with ceremonial verbs.
rules.message: A formal copula alternative may make the sentence heavier without adding meaning.
rules.suggestion: Try 'is', 'has', or a concrete action verb.

rules.name: Verbose connective
rules.description: Long connective phrases can usually be shortened without changing the claim.
rules.message: The phrase is longer than the meaning requires.
rules.suggestion: Use the shorter equivalent unless the cadence is deliberate.

rules.name: Stacked hedge or meta-instruction
rules.description: Multiple qualifiers and 'important to note' phrases weaken rather than calibrate a claim.
rules.message: The sentence hedges or announces importance instead of stating its actual confidence.
rules.suggestion: Use one precise uncertainty marker, or state the evidence and limitation directly.

rules.name: Marketing adjective stack
rules.description: A run of generic product adjectives sounds promotional but says little about behavior.
rules.message: Several generic positive adjectives are stacked together.
rules.suggestion: Keep the one property you can demonstrate and add evidence.
